analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow is caused by out-of-bounds write into perm_value_to_cil[class_index][perm_value]. In cil_classorder_to_policydb(), permission values are assigned incrementally (including inherited common permissions) and then used directly as indices, but there is no bounds check against the fixed allocation size PERMS_PER_CLASS+1 done in cil_binary_create_allocated_pdb(). A class with too many permissions can make sepol_perm->s.value exceed the allocated per-class array length, leading to OOB write at line 357.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzzer input must define class/common permission sets such that, during policydb init, a class accumulates more permissions than PERMS_PER_CLASS (including common + class-specific perms). Data flow: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> cil_build_policydb -> cil_binary_create_allocated_pdb allocates perm_value_to_cil[i] as fixed PERMS_PER_CLASS+1 -> __cil_policydb_init -> cil_classorder_to_policydb writes perm_value_to_cil[class_index][sepol_perm->s.value] without validating sepol_perm->s.value. When value reaches the first index past allocation, ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow.
